name: Jannes
title: Egyptian magician who opposed Moses
summary: Jannes was one of the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses and Aaron at Pharaoh's court when they performed signs and wonders to convince Pharaoh to let the people of Israel go. He is mentioned by name in the New Testament by the apostle Paul as an example of resistance against the truth. Together with Jambres, he became a symbol of false wisdom and opposition to God's will.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to Moses at Pharaoh's court
keyEvents.description: Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses and Aaron when they performed signs before Pharaoh. The Egyptian magicians tried to imitate God's miracles with their magic arts.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the staff turning into a snake
keyEvents.description: When Aaron threw his staff before Pharaoh and it turned into a snake, the Egyptian magicians, including Jannes, imitated this sign with their secret arts, but Aaron's staff swallowed theirs.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the blood in the Nile
keyEvents.description: When Moses and Aaron struck the water of the Nile and it turned to blood, the Egyptian magicians managed to do the same with their arts, which hardened Pharaoh's heart.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the Plague of Frogs
keyEvents.description: When Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and frogs came up, the magicians were able to imitate this sign with their secret arts.

keyEvents.title: Defeat at the Plague of Gnats
keyEvents.description: When Moses and Aaron brought forth gnats from the dust of the earth, the magicians could not imitate this sign and had to admit that this was "the finger of God".

keyEvents.title: Paul's Warning about Opposition to the Truth
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul mentions Jannes and Jambres by name in his second letter to Timothy as examples of people who resisted the truth, with corrupted minds and counterfeit faith. He warns that such people will arise in the last days.
